definition: To succeed in reaching a goal, usually after effort over time.
example: She achieved a perfect score only after months of daily practice.

definition: The way someone thinks and feels about something, shown in how they behave.
example: His attitude towards deadlines changed once he joined a larger team.

definition: To think about something carefully before deciding.
example: The council will consider three different sites before choosing one.

definition: A change that happens because of something else.
example: The medication had no measurable effect on his blood pressure.

definition: To set something up so that it lasts, or to prove that something is true.
example: The company established its first office abroad in 1994.

definition: Facts or signs that show whether something is true.
example: There is little evidence that the policy reduced traffic at all.

definition: The reason something is done, or what it is meant to do.
example: The purpose of the survey was to find out why members were leaving.

definition: Large or important enough to be worth noticing.
example: There was a significant drop in applications after the fee was introduced.

definition: The place, person or thing that something comes from.
example: The report never names the source of its figures.

definition: Relating to study, teaching and research at a university or school.
example: Her academic record was strong enough for any programme she chose.

definition: To admit that something is true, or to show you have noticed someone.
example: The manufacturer finally acknowledged that the fault was its own.

definition: To produce a change in something, or to influence how it develops.
example: Rising fuel prices affect almost every part of the economy.

definition: To accept that something is true without checking it.
example: Do not assume the data is accurate simply because it was published.

definition: Knowing that something exists or is happening.
example: Few passengers were aware that the route had changed that morning.

definition: An advantage gained from something.
example: One benefit of the new schedule is that nobody travels during rush hour.

definition: A sudden important discovery or advance after a period of little progress.
example: The breakthrough came from a technique borrowed from another field.

definition: To put things into groups according to what they have in common.
example: Librarians classify each new title before it reaches the shelves.

definition: Large in amount or degree, enough to matter.
example: Rebuilding the archive took considerable time and money.

definition: To be the parts that something is made of, or to count as something.
example: Women constitute nearly two thirds of the workforce in this sector.

definition: Wanting to know more about something, or strange in an interesting way.
example: A curious detail in the report went unnoticed for months.

definition: To say that something is not true, or to refuse someone what they ask for.
example: The company denied that any customer data had been exposed.

definition: To take something away from someone, or to prevent them from having it.
example: The new rules deprive part-time staff of the same travel allowance.

definition: To decide something officially, or to be the factor that decides an outcome.
example: Rainfall in early spring largely determines the size of the harvest.

definition: Having done something wrong, or feeling bad about having done it.
example: He felt guilty about leaving the work to everyone else.

definition: Happening at once, without any delay.
example: The new rule had an immediate effect on how staff recorded their hours.

definition: Money that a person or organisation regularly receives, usually from work.
example: Households on a low income were hit hardest by the price rise.

definition: Certain to happen and impossible to prevent.
example: Given how quickly the ice is retreating, some flooding is inevitable.

definition: To keep something in the same condition, or to keep saying something is true.
example: The bridge is expensive to maintain but far too useful to close.

definition: To change something slightly, usually to improve it or make it fit.
example: Engineers modified the design after the first round of testing.

definition: Easy to see or understand, needing no explanation.
example: The reason for the delay was obvious the moment we saw the queue.

definition: A plan or suggestion put forward for others to consider.
example: The proposal was rejected twice before anyone read it properly.

definition: To make something smaller in size, amount or degree.
example: Switching to rail reduced the company's emissions by a third.

definition: To get back something you had lost.
example: It took the airline three years to regain the trust of its passengers.

definition: Something that solves a problem or cures an illness.
example: There is no simple remedy for a shortage that took decades to build.

definition: To need something, or to officially demand it.
example: The course requires no previous knowledge of statistics.

definition: To make something more powerful, more solid or harder to break.
example: Steel cables were added to strengthen the roof before winter.

definition: A long effort against something difficult.
example: Keeping the clinic open has been a struggle since the funding was cut.

definition: As much as is needed.
example: Suspicion alone is not sufficient grounds for an investigation.

definition: A habit of behaving in a certain way, or a general direction of change.
example: There is a tendency to blame the software when the process is at fault.

definition: Worth a lot of money, or very useful and important.
example: The interviews turned out to be the most valuable part of the study.

definition: To be different from one another, or to change over time.
example: Prices vary considerably between the coast and the interior.

definition: Found over a large area or among many people.
example: The practice was widespread long before anyone tried to regulate it.

definition: So unreasonable that it seems ridiculous.
example: It seemed absurd to close the only library in a town of ten thousand.

definition: Enough for what is needed, though not more than that.
example: The lighting was adequate for reading but too dim for detailed work.

definition: To state officially, usually in writing, that something is true or meets a standard.
example: Only an approved inspector can certify that the wiring is safe.

definition: Covering everything that is relevant, leaving nothing out.
example: The inspectors produced a comprehensive account of what went wrong.

definition: To say or show the opposite of something else, so both cannot be true.
example: The new figures contradict everything the earlier study concluded.

definition: Good enough to be acceptable, or honest and fair in behaviour.
example: They finally found a decent flat within walking distance of campus.

definition: To separate one thing from another it was joined to.
example: You can detach the keyboard and use the screen on its own.

definition: The cause of someone losing their power, position or success.
example: Overexpansion into markets it did not understand proved the chain's downfall.

definition: To give someone the right to have or do something.
example: The ticket entitles you to one free refill during the performance.

definition: To provide someone or something with what is needed for a task.
example: The course is meant to equip graduates for work in a laboratory.

definition: To develop gradually into something different.
example: What began as a student project evolved into a national service.

definition: One of several things that together cause a result.
example: Cost was only one factor in the decision to close the branch.

definition: To suggest something without stating it directly.
example: Her silence seemed to imply that she disagreed with the plan.

definition: To give a good reason for something, showing it was right or necessary.
example: The board could not justify the expense to its members.

definition: The amount by which one thing exceeds another, or the empty space at the edge of a page.
example: The motion passed by a margin of just four votes.

definition: Not bad, but clearly not good either.
example: The reviews were mediocre and ticket sales fell within a fortnight.

definition: To notice something, or to understand it in a particular way.
example: Younger customers perceive the brand quite differently from older ones.

definition: To spread through every part of something.
example: A quiet distrust of management had permeated the whole department.

definition: Unwilling to do something, and slow to agree to it.
example: Investors remain reluctant to fund projects with no clear return.

definition: Following one after another without a break.
example: Three successive governments promised the railway and none built it.

definition: Treatment intended to help someone recover from illness or difficulty, usually without surgery.
example: Physical therapy restored most of the movement in his shoulder.

definition: Legally or logically acceptable, and therefore able to be used or relied on.
example: Your ticket is valid for travel on any day except public holidays.

definition: To make someone feel distant or unwelcome, so that support is lost.
example: The pricing change alienated many of the firm's oldest customers.

definition: The quality of going on without interruption or sudden change.
example: Keeping the same manager gave the department badly needed continuity.

definition: The extent to which something is reported, included or protected.
example: Rural areas still have poor mobile coverage despite years of investment.

definition: To get rid of something because it is no longer wanted or useful.
example: The team discarded its first three designs before finding one that worked.

definition: Moving apart, or differing from one another.
example: The two studies reached sharply divergent conclusions from the same data.

definition: To make a process happen faster than it otherwise would.
example: A second reviewer was hired to expedite the approval process.

definition: Clever in an original and surprising way.
example: Her solution was ingenious: two problems solved by removing one wall.

definition: Forming a necessary part of something, so that it cannot be removed.
example: Feedback from users became integral to how the product was designed.

definition: The ability to think, reason and understand difficult ideas.
example: The role demands judgement and patience as much as intellect.

definition: The official power to make legal decisions, or the area where that power applies.
example: The dispute fell outside the jurisdiction of the local court.

definition: To describe or represent someone in a particular way.
example: The article portrays him as a reformer, which his colleagues dispute.

definition: The person who held a job or position before the current one.
example: Unlike her predecessor, she published the budget in full each year.

definition: So expensive or difficult that it prevents something from happening.
example: The cost of storage was prohibitive until batteries became cheaper.

definition: To give up something you hold, such as power, a claim or control.
example: She relinquished her seat on the board after twelve years.

definition: Deep regret for something wrong that you have done.
example: He showed no remorse when the full extent of the damage emerged.

definition: Strong enough to withstand pressure, difficulty or criticism.
example: The findings held up under a robust review by outside experts.

definition: To save something from a situation in which the rest is lost.
example: Little could be salvaged from the archive after the flood.

definition: Strong feeling that someone or something deserves no respect at all.
example: The proposal was met with scorn by almost everyone in the room.

definition: Able to continue over a long period without using up resources or causing lasting damage.
example: Fishing at this rate is not sustainable for more than a decade.

definition: Able to be used for many purposes, or able to do many things well.
example: The material is versatile enough for both packaging and insulation.
